## Overview

**In plain terms.** Did the children offered the intervention say more of the vocabulary they were directly taught than those who were not — and how large, and how certain, is that difference? This model estimates the assigned-arm contrast among children in the fitted observed-data analysis set. Randomisation created exchangeability in the original full randomised cohort, but conditioning on archive inclusion and observed analytic variables can break it. A causal reading of the fitted contrast therefore requires selection not to induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes; extending the result to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity.

LRPITT02 is the available-case modified ITT analysis for taught expressive vocabulary, block 1 (`b1extau`). The estimand is the assigned-arm contrast in the post-score $TE_{\text{post}}$ in the model-specific fitted sample, using the RCT phase only (time 1 $\rightarrow$ time 2).
This model supersedes the pre-#168 taught-expressive ITT model (legacy id LRP74, which conditioned on the standardised-vocabulary cross-baseline — unrelated to the current `lrp-rli-med-074`, which reuses the number 74).

_Identification and sign convention._ Under the locked causal DAG, $G$ is a randomised root, so the offer contrast in the original full randomised cohort requires no baseline-covariate adjustment. This fit instead conditions on archive inclusion and observed analytic variables; a causal reading of $\tau$ in the fitted sample requires that selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and potential outcomes, and extending it to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity. The own baseline $\gamma_{\text{own}}$ and linear age $\gamma_A$ are **precision terms only** — they may sharpen $\tau$ but do not identify effects after selection — and no cross-baseline conditioning is used. Attendance or sessions are never conditioned on (a DAG collider). **Sign convention:** $G = 1$ is the intervention arm, so a **positive** $\tau$ means the intervention arm has the higher modelled outcome.

## Model

$$
\eta_i = \alpha + \tau\, G_i
       + \gamma_{\text{own}}\, \text{logit}_*(TE_{\mathrm{pre},i}, N)
       + \gamma_A\, A_{\text{std},i},
$$

with Beta-Binomial likelihood $TE_{\text{post},i} \sim \text{BetaBinomial}(N, \mu_i\kappa, (1-\mu_i)\kappa)$,
$\mu_i = \sigma(\eta_i)$, $N = 24$. Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.
HSGPs on age and own baseline are off by default (the 2026-04-18 sensitivity
verdict).
